In traditional [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Japan|Japanese cuisine]], miso soup is served for breakfast every day, and often served with meals as well.<ref>{{Cite web |title=特集「目覚めにぴったり!朝の味噌汁」：農林水産省 |url=https://www.maff.go.jp/j/pr/aff/2306/spe1_04.html |access-date=2025-02-01 |trans-title=Special "Wake Up Perfectly! Morning Miso Soup": Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries |language= ja}}</ref>

== Ingredients ==
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Sesame_Oil|sesame oil]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Miso|miso]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Green Onion|green onions]] (optional), finely [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]]
* ½ cake [[Cookbook:Tofu|tofu]] (optional), cut into ½-inch cubes
* 2–3 fresh [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushrooms]] (optional), thinly [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* 5–6 [[Cookbook:Shrimp|shrimp]] (optional), [[Cookbook:Cube|cubed]] or shredded
* Some pieces of [[Cookbook:Seaweed|seaweed]] (optional)

== Procedure ==
# Heat oil in a small pot.
# Add green onion. Cook for a few minutes while stirring frequently.
# Add 2 ½ cups of water. Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].
# Dissolve miso in remaining ½ cup of water and add to pot.
# Lower heat and add mushrooms, seaweed, and tofu, if desired.
